scenes.headline: How SGLang keeps its KV cache in a tree
scenes.sub: RadixAttention, and the scheduler that keeps it warm.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Marigold! SGLang began as a language for programs that fork. Here's why its KV cache is a tree.

scenes.text: RadixAttention indexes the KV cache with a radix tree over token prefixes. Requests that share a prefix share one path, and a node splits where they diverge.
scenes.mark: a node splits where they diverge
scenes.say: The idea: a radix tree over token prefixes. Requests that share a prefix share one path, and split where they diverge.

steps.say: A new prompt is matched down the tree. A shared system prompt is one node, with one reference count.
When a second chat diverges, the node splits right there, so both sessions share the prompt.

steps.note: lock_ref: locked prefixes leave the evictable pool
steps.say: A prefix an in-flight request needs is locked out of the evictable pool. Not recent: ineligible.
Eviction runs off a priority heap, and cascades: a parent left childless and unlocked becomes a candidate too.

scenes.title: The scheduler keeps the tree warm

items.text: Sort the queue by longest prefix
items.say: The scheduler decides what's cached by picking what runs. Longest prefix match runs the best-cached request first.
A near-duplicate still waiting in the queue goes to the back, so its sibling fills the tree and it returns as a hit.

items.text: Opt in: the default is FCFS
items.say: It's opt in. The default is first come, first served, and LPM switches off above a hundred and twenty-eight queued.

scenes.title: Prefill tokens, three chats
scenes.note: the article's simulation; the gap closes as the budget grows
scenes.say: In the article's simulation, three chats and a small cache, longest prefix first cuts prefill two point six eight times.

left.title: Token mask
items: One bitmask row per request, every step
Illegal logits set to negative infinity
left.say: What ships is a token mask: each step, every illegal logit is set to negative infinity before sampling.

right.title: Jump-forward decoding
items: Appends forced spans with no forward pass
Defined in every backend, called by none
right.say: The paper's famous jump-forward trick emits forced spans with no forward pass. Every grammar backend defines it; nothing calls it.

scenes.text: SGLang's cache is shaped like its language: a tree, because programs fork. The language faded; the tree stayed.
scenes.say: So the cache is shaped like the language. A tree, because programs fork.

recap: A radix tree: shared prefixes share one path
Locked prefixes can't be evicted; eviction cascades up
Longest-prefix scheduling makes a small cache act big
scenes.say: To recap: a prefix tree, locks on what's in use, and a scheduler that keeps it warm.
